name: Yates Row
description: A barbell bent-over row variation using a supinated (underhand) grip, popularized by bodybuilder Dorian Yates. The reverse grip shifts the loading emphasis from the upper lats toward the lower lats and biceps, and the torso is typically held at a less horizontal angle than a standard bent-over row.

execution.starting_position: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip, shoulder-width. Hinge forward to approximately 70 degrees from vertical.
execution.setup_instructions: Load a barbell on the floor or use a rack. Grip the bar underhand (palms up). Hinge forward to the working angle.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core hard and hold the torso at approximately 70 degrees from vertical.
Step 2: Pull the bar toward the lower abdomen or navel, keeping the elbows close to the body.
Step 3: Squeeze the lats and biceps at the top of the movement.
Step 4: Lower the bar under control to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Letting the torso excessively rise during the pull — maintain the forward lean
Using too much bicep and not enough lat engagement
safety_considerations: The underhand grip is naturally stronger than overhand — expect to use more weight than a standard row
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom. Bar pulled to lower abdomen at the top.
coaching_cues: Elbows stay close to the body
